Question: with labels, unlabeled data and the predictor fixed, how much shorter can an interval for a mean be than PPI++? -Prediction-powered inference (PPI) turns a fixed predictor into a valid confidence interval for a mean, and PPI++ is its strongest form when the labels, the unlabeled records and the predictor are given. We ask how much shorter such an interval can be without changing any of the three. Classical semi-supervised theory gives a variance floor; we write the exact gap between PPI++ and it, which vanishes if and only if the regression of the outcome on the prediction is affine, and a break-even label count above which learning a calibrated control variate from the same labels pays.
